checkFromNote: Entries before this commit recorded the hash of the changelog commit rather than the commit they describe, so they cannot be verified by hash. changelog:check only polices commits after this one.

entries.message: Joint Display: stop the description asserting an interviews-only design
entries.summary: The real-mode page description read 'The design is interviews-only, so rows are the five groups interviewed rather than evidence types'. That is no longer true: focus groups are collected, and the page's own evidence-type filter offers all three types. Rather than swapping one hardcoded composition for another, the description now explains the row semantics without asserting which types exist — a segment lands in a row by who said it rather than by which evidence type it came from, so a row aggregates whatever that stakeholder group said in an interview or a focus group alike, and the filter is there to read one type on its own. Because it makes no claim about composition it cannot go stale as the corpus changes. It also drops the hardcoded 'five', which the Rows shown card already lists and which the row toggles above can change. Synthetic mode's description is untouched; pages and exports verified identical.

entries.message: Joint Display: derive the evidence-type claim from the corpus
entries.summary: The 'What this analysis can and cannot claim' card asserted that 'documents and focus groups have not been collected, so only the interview rows are populated'. Against the live corpus — five focus groups, no interviews, no documents — that was exactly backwards: the page denied the existence of the only evidence type actually held, in the card whose whole purpose is stating what may be claimed. The sentence is now derived from countsByType through a new evidenceCoverage helper, which separates types that are collected (any session) from types that are populated (any coded segment), since an entered-but-uncoded source contributes nothing to the matrix. Three cases are worded distinctly: nothing coded, exactly one populated type, or several. The 'Still required' bullet reads the same source and drops its trailing clause once every type is collected. evidenceCoverage, listTypes and sentenceCase sit beside countsByType in engine/sources.js so the Visualisations caption making the same claim can read the same derivation instead of a copy; countsByType now also carries each type's plural label for that prose. Synthetic mode is unchanged: pages and exports verified identical.

entries.message: Delete a real session, and everything derived from it
entries.summary: Removing a single imported session — an interview, focus group or document — previously required editing localStorage by hand. Real mode now has a delete that names what it destroys before doing it: the session and its verbatim text, the coded segments derived from it, and the override-log entries recorded against those segments, each counted from the live workspace rather than described in general terms. It is deliberately hard to fire: the button opens a panel instead of acting, and 'Delete permanently' stays disabled until the session's own label is typed exactly; Cancel writes nothing. The cascade now includes overridesLog, which the previous delete left behind pointing at segments that no longer existed. Nothing else is touched — other sessions, participant records, codebook and protocol are all verified intact by id after deletion. Coding, Reliability, Pattern-Matching and the Export Centre corpus table derive their totals from the workspace on every render, so all four read correctly straight after a delete with no re-code click; re-coding the remaining evidence stays an explicit action. Synthetic mode keeps its original one-step delete on a separate function: sharing one path behind a mode flag is how this eventually destroys irreplaceable data on the wrong branch, and hardening synthetic's path would itself have been a synthetic-mode change.

entries.message: Say "interviews" only where interviews are what is meant
entries.summary: The Coding page's action button counted every uncoded evidence source and then called them all interviews, so a researcher with two focus groups and a policy document queued was told they had three uncoded interviews. The label now reads the actual mix from sourceTypeOf: 'Code 3 uncoded sources (1 individual interview, 1 focus group, 1 document)' when several types are waiting, or the type named directly — 'Code 1 uncoded individual interview' — when only one is. A grep for the same pattern found two further real-mode strings using 'interview' to mean any evidence source: Coding's 'No interviews to code' and Pattern-Matching's 'code some interviews', both now saying evidence in real mode. Deliberately left alone: JointDisplay and PilotReport, which were already mode-conditional; and Run Interviews, Persona Builder, Persona Library, Reliability's pilot note and the AI review log, where the corpus genuinely is interviews only. Synthetic wording is unchanged throughout — synthetic mode has one evidence type, so 'interview' is accurate there rather than a leftover; pages and exports verified identical.

entries.message: Import: say what landed and where it went
entries.summary: After a bulk CSV import the banner said only 'Imported N sources from <file>', so confirming what had actually landed meant navigating to Transcripts and deducing it from a date-sorted list. The summary now breaks the import down by evidence type and names every source — '2 individual interviews — P05, P06 / 1 focus group — Managers / 1 document — Council minutes 2024' — and links to /fieldwork/transcripts?new=<ids>, which shows exactly those records with one click back to the full corpus. To make that possible applyImportPlan's 'imported' return changed from an array of label strings to {id, sourceType, label} per source; its only consumer was the banner's count. Focus-group labels resolve through focusGroupLabel so the summary shows 'Managers', not 'fg-managers'. A focus group whose group already holds a session still defaults to skip under the existing overwrite guard and is therefore correctly absent from the summary. Synthetic mode does not have import of this kind and is unchanged; pages and exports verified identical.

entries.message: Transcripts: filter the corpus by evidence type
entries.summary: Transcripts listed interviews, focus groups and documents in one flat chip row, so reading one evidence type meant knowing by name which chips belonged to it. Real mode now has a tab per type — All / Individual interviews / Focus groups / Documentary sources — each showing its own count, with the selection held in the URL as ?type= so a filtered view can be linked or bookmarked. Selecting a tab clears the chosen transcript so the detail pane cannot show a session the filter excludes. An empty tab keeps the tabs rendered and reports where the rest of the corpus is, rather than collapsing to the no-transcripts-yet state, which now fires only when the corpus is genuinely empty. Filtering reuses sourceTypeOf and SOURCE_TYPES rather than introducing a second notion of evidence type. The page also reads a ?new= list of session ids, inert until the import summary links into it. Synthetic mode has one evidence type and is unchanged: no tabs, same flat list, pages and exports verified identical.

entries.message: Transcripts and Export Centre read the corpus by evidence type
entries.summary: Transcripts named every session by personaName and numbered every answer 'Q{n}', so a focus group showed under a participant name with its turns numbered as interview questions and no speaker rendered at all — the speaker was stored, never displayed. Sessions now use sessionLabel; a focus-group turn leads with its speaker code and the FG question that prompted it (numbered from the live focus group protocol, so reordering renumbers the transcript) or 'not on the schedule'; documents head extracts as extracts and carry document type and period. Export Centre showed only a pooled transcript count in the pre-export consent dialog, which conceals that one focus-group file carries several people's words: real mode now shows a corpus-by-evidence-type table above the export buttons and the confirmation itemises the same breakdown, both from countsByType so page, dialog and Pilot Report cannot disagree. Documents show '—' for people rather than 0. Synthetic mode unchanged in both, verified by diffing re-exported report and appendix against pre-change exports.

entries.message: Focus groups run their own protocol, not the interview schedule
entries.summary: Focus groups no longer borrow the nine interview questions. A second instrument lives in the workspace as focusGroupProtocol and is edited on Interview Protocol → Focus group protocol, a tab that appears in real mode only — synthetic mode runs no focus groups and its protocol page is unchanged. Five RQ-mapped questions written to make participants talk to each other, with their own opening and closing scripts and their own Restore default 5, edited independently of the interview protocol and persisted. Turn entry gains an optional 'Prompted by' selector over those five, so a turn that answers nothing on the schedule stays blank rather than being forced onto a question; the focus-group entry page now shows the protocol itself. Extended-long CSV import reads questionNumber on focus-group rows against the focus group protocol (1-5, blank allowed, out-of-range blocks the row) and the downloaded template carries the live FG question text. Saved workspaces are back-filled in mergeWithDefaults.

entries.message: Participant Records: no default stakeholder group
entries.summary: The Add-participant form no longer defaults to Senior leader. It opens on a '— choose stakeholder group —' placeholder and Add stays disabled until a group is chosen, since the group decides focus-group eligibility and the joint-display row. senior-leader remains in STAKEHOLDER_GROUPS and in no focus-group roster. Editing an existing record still prefills its group.

entries.message: Focus groups: revised roster mapping
entries.summary: FOCUS_GROUP_ELIGIBILITY updated: academic board takes multi-role and academic, managers gains academic, so multi-role is eligible for three groups and academic for two. The allocation marker re-checks eligibility per membership rather than counting, so multiple legitimate memberships read as muted 'also in' with no override prompt; only memberships the mapping does not account for turn red. senior-leader is now eligible for no focus group while remaining the Add-participant default — reported, not changed.

entries.message: Rename the third focus group to Academic Board members
entries.summary: fg-heads-of-departments becomes fg-academic-board with the label 'Academic Board members'. Saved focus-group sessions are migrated on load via RENAMED_FOCUS_GROUPS in mergeWithDefaults: focusGroupId and display name are rewritten while the session id is preserved so coded segments stay joined. Verified against a workspace forced back to the old id.

entries.message: Focus groups: the supplied roster mapping
entries.summary: FOCUS_GROUP_ELIGIBILITY filled with the researcher's five rosters; every focus group now greys non-members. multi-role is explicitly eligible in shareholders-and-board and external-agents, so the undetermined placeholder state is removed. A prior membership the mapping accounts for is reported neutrally as 'also in', not as a double-allocation error; unaccounted-for memberships stay red. The unsupplied-roster notice is dropped as unreachable.

entries.message: Focus groups: attendee chips carry role and existing allocation
entries.summary: Attendee chips in focus-group entry now show code, stakeholder group, role descriptor where the record holds one, and a red marker naming any other focus group the participant is already saved into, so double-allocation is visible before it happens. Participant records hold no name field by design, so the role descriptor is the most identifying detail available.

entries.message: Focus groups: the attendee picker reflects each participant's group
entries.summary: Step 2 of focus-group entry now reads the participant record's stakeholder group. FOCUS_GROUP_ELIGIBILITY in src/data/seeds.js holds the roster rules; four of five are null pending the researcher, and only the given rule is encoded (agent belongs to the external group and no internal one). Ineligible participants are greyed with their group as the reason, never hidden, and remain selectable behind a confirm. Multi-role participants are marked undetermined rather than greyed.

entries.message: Focus groups: switching group clears the attendees and turns beneath it
entries.summary: Choosing a different focus group in step 1 resets the attendee list and the turns, which belong to the session being left. A switch with typed turn text asks for confirmation first, naming both groups and the number of turns at stake; declining leaves the group, attendees and text untouched.

entries.message: Fifth focus group: external parties (recruitment agents)
entries.summary: FOCUS_GROUPS gains fg-external-agents, marked external. Transcript Entry warns on selection that this group's members are outside the institution and its consent and confidentiality terms differ. Session labels, the import template and import validation follow the array with no change.

entries.message: Real mode 5/5: corpus by evidence type, and import for all three types
entries.summary: Pilot Report and Chapter-3 appendix report the corpus per evidence type (sessions/sources, participants, coded segments); documentary rows count sources and documentary contributors are labelled as such. Bulk import gains an extended long layout with sourceType and source columns, with its own template: focus-group turns must name a speaker, document rows must not, and every violation blocks the whole file at preview. Wide and plain-long imports unchanged; synthetic mode byte-identical apart from timestamps.

entries.message: Real mode 4/5: attribute focus-group turns and documentary evidence
entries.summary: Focus-group turns count under their speaker's stakeholder group row; document segments aggregate into a new 'Documentary evidence' row appended after the five stakeholder rows in real mode, counted in sources rather than participants. Pattern-Matching and the Joint Display gain a per-evidence-type view filter (all / interviews / focus groups / documents), kept out of stored settings deliberately. Reliability reports kappa overall and split by evidence type on the same substantive base. Synthetic mode byte-identical apart from generation timestamps.

entries.message: Real mode 3/5: code focus-group turns and document extracts
entries.summary: Focus-group and document segments run through the same codebook, dual-pass coding, tie handling and override column; focus-group segments carry their speaker so they attribute to that person, and non-answer detection is skipped for documents where the interview disclaimer heuristic would misfire.

entries.message: Real mode 2/5: enter focus-group turns and document extracts
entries.summary: Transcript Entry gains an evidence-type selector with turn-based focus-group entry, where a turn without a speaker cannot be saved, and document entry carrying title, type and period with no participant.

entries.message: Real mode 1/5: source types for focus groups and documentary evidence
entries.summary: Adds the interview/focus-group/document source-type vocabulary, the four fixed focus groups and the six document types, and migrates existing real records to the interview type.

entries.message: Joint Display: real-mode rows are stakeholder groups, not evidence types
entries.summary: Real mode's pattern-matching matrix now has one row per stakeholder group with membership taken from the participant record, drops the uncollected evidence-type placeholder rows, and names any participant whose group maps to no row instead of assigning one.

entries.message: Flag stored study-design prose that still describes a synthetic pilot
entries.summary: The Pilot Report's synthetic-sounding Section 1 is researcher-edited workspace text, not a hardcoded string, so the app now flags it in real mode on the Study Design page and at export rather than rewriting it.

entries.message: Coding: carry manual overrides and the override log across a re-code
entries.summary: Re-coding discarded every manual override and emptied the override log with it; overrides are now re-attached by segment id, the log is preserved, and re-coding with overrides present confirms first and says how many it will keep.

entries.message: Reliability: compute kappa over substantive segments and state the exclusion
entries.summary: Cohen's kappa now excludes detected non-answers, which agreed with themselves by construction and inflated the figure; the page and every export report the substantive base, the excluded count and the reason, and substantive-but-unclassified segments are deliberately kept in.

entries.message: Real coding: detect non-answers explicitly instead of force-coding them
entries.summary: Role disclaimers were scoring against code definitions through shared procedural vocabulary and manufacturing guaranteed disagreements; they are now detected before scoring, marked non-answer and left unclassified, with a conservative rule that keeps any answer carrying substantive content.

entries.message: Real coding: resolve score ties by code label, not by internal id
entries.summary: Equal-scoring codes were resolved by internal id string, so deleting and re-adding a code changed coding output; ties now resolve by code label and are recorded and displayed on the segment rather than silently decided.

entries.message: Joint Display: make the evidence-type rows selectable, per mode
entries.summary: Evidence-type rows can be switched off from the Joint Display page, independently per workspace mode; hidden rows disappear from the table, the heatmap and every export while keeping their expected-evidence text, and an all-off matrix shows an explicit empty state.

entries.message: Make every synthetic label mode-aware across the analysis pages and exports
entries.summary: Page tags, sidebar subtitle, chart watermarks and captions, the Joint Display claims list and the seed-based reliability panels now follow the workspace mode instead of asserting synthetic provenance over real participant data; synthetic mode verified byte-identical.

entries.message: Coding: show Before → Now on a decided proposal, not Current vs Proposed
entries.summary: An accepted definition proposal no longer displays identical text under Current and Proposed: decided rows read the before-text from the decision log and show Before against Now, with the model's original wording kept visible when the researcher edited it.

entries.message: Backfill six missing Change Log entries and make log-change commit its own work
entries.summary: Restores entries for the six commits whose changelog updates were written and then discarded before commit, and makes log-change commit the entry it writes; adds changelog:check and explains why a git post-commit hook is the wrong tool here.

entries.message: Real mode: accept, edit or reject AI-proposed codebook definition changes
entries.summary: Definition proposals from the disagreement diagnostic can be accepted, edited before accepting, or rejected, with every decision logged with before/after text; structural proposals are surfaced as design decisions with no apply action, and no coded segment is ever re-coded.

entries.message: Real mode: allow configuring the OpenAI key, and diagnose blocked requests
entries.summary: The OpenAI key, live-AI toggle and model pickers are available in real mode behind a warning that running the diagnostic transmits participant answer text; a blocked request now reports the three causes that produce Failed to fetch instead of the bare message.

entries.message: Real mode: AI diagnostic for coder disagreements (read-only)
entries.summary: Adds a read-only Coding-page diagnostic that asks the configured OpenAI model why the two coding passes disagree, behind a per-use confirm naming the data transmission; it writes no code, override or definition, and real-mode AI log entries now live in the local-only real slice so prompts quoting participants never sync.

entries.message: Real mode: bulk transcript import from CSV/TSV with a mandatory preview
entries.summary: Adds file-based transcript import for real mode in wide (one row per participant) and long (one row per answer) layouts, with a hand-written RFC 4180 reader, a live-protocol CSV template, a mandatory preview resolving unknown codes, duplicates and existing transcripts, and an all-or-nothing single-commit write.

entries.message: Real mode: edit participant records, including the participant code
entries.summary: Adds a per-row Edit action for real participant records covering code, stakeholder group, role descriptor and tenure band; changing the code carries the denormalised copy on transcripts, coded segments and the override log with it, so no data is orphaned.

entries.message: Real data mode 4/4: confidentiality header on real exports, confirm before export
entries.summary: Real-mode exports carry a confidentiality header instead of the synthetic caveat, name what is being exported before writing the file, and exclude the synthetic corpus; import, live AI, calibration and demo data are unavailable in real mode.

entries.message: Real data mode 3/4: code real transcripts from the text alone
entries.summary: Real-mode coding never consults a pre-assigned hypothesis: both passes classify from the answer text against the whole codebook, unmatched text stays unclassified, and the pages state that two machine passes are not inter-rater reliability.

entries.message: Real data mode 2/4: participant records, transcript entry, mode-scoped nav
entries.summary: Adds pseudonymised real-participant records (no name, no weight profile, no held propositions) and a per-question transcript entry screen with no generation; synthetic and real pages are mutually exclusive in the nav; all analysis reads/writes go through the mode-scoped accessors.
